pr.title: Sign a pull request off only when every reviewing model is clean
pr.head: 5015a7f81d539f88cbc73538f5c2ba962ca6177b

summary: A Projector review loop reviews every head pushed to the operator's pull requests and publishes each review with project review publish. Every review posts as one GitHub account. On the operator's own pull request, GitHub allows only a COMMENT review, so the draft state carries the outcome: draft means the head isn't signed off, and ready means it is. This pull request is the third layer of the multi-model review work. The two earlier layers, now merged to main, let several models, such as Claude and Codex, review one pull request side by side without colliding.

Without this layer, publish still sets the draft state from its own verdict alone. If Codex requested changes and Claude then found the head clean, Claude's publish marked the pull request ready, and Codex's objection disappeared from the pull-request list. Now every publish applies one sign-off rule over GitHub's state after it submits, so the last model to finish sees every verdict and sets the final draft state.

Sign-offWhenDraft state on a self-review
changes-requestedAny model's newest verdict on the head requests changes.Draft
waitingNo model requests changes, but a model is still reviewing the head or a Projector finding thread is open.Left as it is
cleanEvery model's newest verdict on the head is clean, no model is reviewing, and no thread is open.Ready, after the peer wait
unreviewedNo model has a verdict on the head.Never the result of a publish

A model is reviewing a head while its start comment there is live. A start comment is the comment setup posts when a review begins. It stops being live once its model posts a verdict on that head, or a day after it was last edited. The rule also adds a peer wait: a loop that hasn't noticed a push yet has posted nothing, so before publish marks a draft ready, it waits up to review.peer_wait seconds (180 by default) for any model that reviewed an earlier head. A new project review status command prints the rule's result, and fix-pr now reads it to decide whether a head is clean.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Model: the reviewer's identity within one account, the model ID a review marker records, such as claude-opus-5-5, lowercased and without a bracketed variant such as [1m].
  • Start comment: the comment project review setup posts when a review begins. Its marker names the head and the model.
  • Peer: another model that has a verdict on an earlier head, or a live start comment on another head, and nothing on this one.
  • Sign-off: the rule's result for a head: clean, changes-requested, waiting, or unreviewed.

cards.title: What this layer leaves for later
cards.html:
• Adopting a stopped model's findings, project review adopt, and census --wait belong to the next layer. Here a clean verdict still needs every finding thread closed, so this layer only ever makes the sign-off more conservative.
  • The plan, docs/projects/multi-model-review/readme.md, stays in-progress.
  • Two P2 threads from the review of bd07831 remain open at this rebased head: fix-pr's clean test can't see another account's Projector loop, and one docs/cli.md sentence about incremental reviews is stale.

groups.title: The sign-off rule and the peer wait
groups.kicker: How review.py decides a head's sign-off from GitHub's state, and how publish uses it
intro: Every publish now ends by asking one question about the head it published on: is every model that's reviewing it satisfied? models_on groups the reviewer account's Projector verdicts and live start comments by model. signoff turns that grouping, plus the count of open finding threads, into one of the four results in the overview table.

The peer wait sits in sign. While the rule says clean and a peer is pending, it reads GitHub again every 15 seconds until the deadline: review.peer_wait seconds after this review began on the head. A peer's start comment turns the result into waiting, a peer's verdict joins the rule, and a peer that posts nothing by the deadline is treated as absent. A head that moves during the wait ends it, and publish then leaves the draft state alone for the new head's reviews to decide.

On another author's pull request, publish still leaves the draft state alone. The rule decides only whether a clean verdict may post an APPROVE where review.allow_approve is true. GitHub's reviewDecision follows one account's newest approval or change request, so one model's approval would erase another model's standing change request. publish therefore runs the rule before it submits, counting its own verdict as posted.

checks.text: The rule runs after the submit so that two models finishing together still sign off. Each one sees the other's start comment as live until the other has submitted, so only the publish that runs last can reach clean.

files.note: Adds models_on, signoff, pending_peers, peer_wait, sign, status, and status_lines. publish now applies the rule after it submits and records whether the review was a self-review. The unused self_review helper is gone.

checks.text: models_on keeps each model's newest verdict on this head (verdict) and its newest verdict on another head (earlier), plus a live start comment on this head (reviewing) or on another head (elsewhere). Liveness comes from is_live, which the layer below added.

Checked the order of the tests against plan § 2.3. Any change request wins over everything else. A reviewing model or an open thread gives waiting. Otherwise, at least one verdict gives clean, and none gives unreviewed. SignoffTests covers each branch.
The head-moved check runs only after a sleep. A publish that never waits applies the rule to the head it published on, which matches what publish did before this change.
The deadline counts from head_started_at: when setup posted the start comment, or when move edited it for this head. A review that already took longer than review.peer_wait doesn't wait at all.

The approval check before the submit can wait up to review.peer_wait. If the head moves during that wait, the review still posts a COMMENT on the old head without checking again. The review is accurate for that commit. The review body lists this as a suggestion.

Only a self-review on a draft waits. A ready pull request and another author's pull request pass now() as the deadline, so sign returns after one read. This read counts this review's own verdict only once reviewer_reviews lists it. Until then, the review's own start comment reads as live. The review body suggests passing the posted review in, as the approval check does.

files.note: Adds project review status. Reads review.peer_wait from the review's checkout before publish runs, and prints the sign-off, how long publish waited, and which peers never posted.

checks.text: status finds the reviewer the way setup does: --reviewer, then review.username from the checkout it runs in, then the authenticated user. It counts only that account's verdicts.
A bad review.peer_wait refuses before anything is posted. PeerWaitTests passes "180", -1, true, and 1.5, and checks that the lock stays held and no review is posted.

files.note: SignoffTests, PeerWaitTests, CrossAuthorSignoffTests, and StatusTests, on the fake GitHub with a fake clock that the peer wait's sleeps advance.

groups.title: Skills that read the sign-off
groups.kicker: review-pr, fix-pr, and start-fix-loop describe the rule in place of a single verdict
intro: A self-review's draft state no longer means one model's verdict. It means the sign-off of every model that's reviewing the head. review-pr renames its section to "Draft means the head is not signed off" and states the rule and the peer wait. It also asks the review to run publish with a timeout of at least review.peer_wait plus two minutes.

fix-pr used to call a head clean when a clean verdict named it. Now it asks project review status, so a head that one model passed while another model is still reviewing isn't reported clean. start-fix-loop's DRAFT line now clears when every reviewing model has signed off.

files.note: The sign-off rule, the peer wait, and status under "Review as one model among several". The publish modes and the report now name the sign-off.
The clean test reads project review status.

checks.text: Open P2 finding: status counts only verdicts from review.username or the authenticated user. When another account's Projector loop reviews the operator's pull request, status reports unreviewed for a head that loop found clean, so fix-pr never reports the head clean. The suggested fix passes --reviewer with the login that posted the Projector verdicts.

files.note: DRAFT clears once every reviewing model signs off.

The plan's status table now says that a model's verdict entry carries its sha and that a start comment entry carries its comment_sha, which is what the code returns.
